name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 43

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Depression nearly impoverished area of city

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an economic depression or downturn

explanation.surface: A recession leaves a run-down part of town even poorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a squalid, overcrowded district of a town, typically home to the poor.

clue.text: Embargo faced by old port

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: A trade embargo imposed on a historic harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'faced by' puts the old letter on top, ahead of the embargo word. Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a real Scottish harbour town, so a specific example of a port.

clue.text: Sun above horse causing problem

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday or on a compass of planets
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: Hot sunshine overhead is making trouble for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' places the sun letter before the horse in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected hitch or difficulty, a synonym for problem.

clue.text: Lakes south of wild gorge offering food

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the following word's letters run riot
in a down entry, south of means placed underneath, so the lakes come last

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Lakes below a rugged ravine providing something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a canyon or like eating greedily; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg roll is a fried snack of filling wrapped in egg-based pastry, so an example of food.

clue.text: Nervous lady began to entertain queen? Generally

indicators.note: something nervous is jittery and agitated, so the following letters are jumbled
to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An anxious woman began hosting royalty, at least for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen's letter sits inside the rearranged letters, just before the final G and E.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning on the whole, in general, so it swaps for generally.

clue.text: Irresponsible speed by man on board, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the chess word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to fly is to speed along
taken as written
a knight is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A reckless driver racing past someone on a ship or bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a passenger or crew member; it is a chess man, and the chess piece sounds like the hours of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-by-night describes an unreliable, shady operator who may vanish without paying, hence irresponsible.

clue.text: Forthright worker found below ditch

blocks.note: a trench is a long ditch
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An honest labourer turns up at the bottom of a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'found below' puts the worker under the ditch, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and vigorously direct in expression, close to forthright or outspoken.

clue.text: Artist, unknown character in foreign state

indicators.note: in places the unknown character inside the foreign state's name

blocks.note: Goa is a state of India, foreign from a British point of view
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A painter turns out to be a mysterious figure living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown character' sounds like a stranger; in crosswords it is an algebraic letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter, so an example of an artist.

clue.text: Denver, perhaps? Wind goes about it — and squally air!

indicators.note: goes about means wraps around, so the wind word surrounds what follows
squally weather is gusty and turbulent, so the letters are blown into a new order

blocks.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
taken as written
the word air, rearranged

explanation.surface: Is Denver, the windy mile-high city, buffeted by squalls?
explanation.walkthrough: Denver suggests the Colorado city; it is John Denver, the folk singer who accompanied himself on guitar. The wind word splits to hold both other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: John Denver performed with an acoustic guitar, so he is an example of a guitar player, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Anémigré possibly keeping European animals for exhibition

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered
keeping means holding on to, so the rearranged letters hold the extra one inside

blocks.note: the words an émigré run together, accents dropped
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An exile perhaps keeps a private collection of European beasts on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan ran 'An émigré' together; the two words together are the letters to rearrange, with the European letter tucked in after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for public display, as in a travelling show.

clue.text: A taxing body making appearance

blocks.note: taken as written
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A tax office putting in an appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK government department that collected income tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a person's manner or look, as in an air of confidence, so it means appearance.

clue.text: For retirement, a top island

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
No. 1, written NO plus the numeral as I, means the top one

explanation.surface: A first-class island chosen as a retirement home.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 1 doubles as the letter I. Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a specific Scottish island, so an example of an island.

clue.text: Tough sort organised teachers

blocks.note: first meaning: a hard case, a tough person, as in a hard one to crack
second meaning: the initials of the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union

explanation.surface: A hard-nosed type got the teachers into a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' here means unionised; the National Union of Teachers is a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard nut is a tough person; the teachers' union is known by its three-letter initials.

clue.text: Supposedly clever figure spilling cream last

indicators.note: spilt things scatter about and land in a mess, so the letters are scattered too

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A know-all knocks over the cream at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is someone who thinks they are cleverer than they are, an irritating know-all.

clue.text: Skilled worker and mate son twice confused

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so all the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the word son written two times

explanation.surface: A craftsman and his partner are bewildered by two sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'twice' means son counts two times, giving ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason cuts and dresses stone for building, a trade requiring long apprenticeship and skill.

clue.text: A farm building set up to house produce? Part of ancient society

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means raised from the bottom, so the building is read upwards
to house means to give a home to, so the produce goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a crop is produce from the land
a silo is a tower on a farm for storing grain

explanation.surface: A grain store built to hold harvest, a relic of an old farming community.
explanation.walkthrough: A and the upturned silo together house the produce word, which sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis was the fortified upper citadel of an ancient Greek city-state, so a part of that ancient community.

clue.text: Prat foolishly detaining actor and entertainer

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving without order, so the letters are scrambled
detaining means holding someone in, so the scrambled letters hold the inner piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
as printed this word cannot supply the inner letters; the wordplay needs a dance here

explanation.surface: A fool clumsily holds up an actor and a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged fool's letters must go round DANCE, but the printed 'actor' does not give it; the clue was probably misprinted or misread, and the answer comes from definition and crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap dancer performs on stage in metal-soled shoes, so is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Woman without second colleague

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: Sally is a woman's name
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A woman left without a supporting co-worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' asks for any female name; the right one is the name that starts with the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or associate on the same side, close to a colleague.

clue.text: Company car put for renovation? It's not honest

indicators.note: renovation means doing something up anew, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm's car is put in for a makeover, but something dishonest is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car put' looks like the letters to rearrange; only 'put' is, while the car is a Rolls-Royce, known by its two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt means dishonest, especially open to bribery, so it fits a description of something not honest.

clue.text: Roman street cuts charge for luxury food

indicators.note: a road that cuts into something runs through its middle, so it goes inside

blocks.note: something in your care is your charge
via is Latin for road or street

explanation.surface: A Roman road slices through the price of a delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a fee; it is charge as in responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare, an older spelling of caviar, is sturgeon roe, the classic expensive delicacy.

clue.text: Acknowledge song first? Have a rest!

blocks.note: a lied is a German art song
to own is to admit or acknowledge

explanation.surface: Admit the song comes first, then take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the song word goes ahead of the acknowledging word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to recline, typically to rest, so it works as an instruction to have a rest.

clue.text: Casual worker among diligent employees

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: One stand-in worker on a staff of hard grafters.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary employee, typically from an agency, hence casual.

clue.text: Well-known Greek reforming a lost rite

indicators.note: reforming means forming again in a new shape, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous Greek is reviving a forgotten ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle, pupil of Plato and tutor to Alexander, is among the most famous ancient Greek philosophers.

clue.text: Valuable material derived from timeless work

indicators.note: timeless here means without its time abbreviation, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: toil is hard work

explanation.surface: Precious stuff produced by a classic, enduring work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' looks like praise for the work; it means minus T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is a precious raw material, often called black gold.

clue.text: Possess dress that's not good

indicators.note: that's not means lacking, so the letter named next is dropped

blocks.note: a gown is a long dress
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Owning a frock that is not up to much.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it as your property, a synonym of possess.

clue.text: Pull provided by room, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means what reaches the ear, so a word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: Influence offered by a room, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' looks like a noun for influence; it is the verb, to drag. In British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something is to pull or drag it with effort.

clue.text: I call ads confused about a hundred cars

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters are mixed
about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the number

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled by adverts for a hundred cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The hundred goes in before the final S of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadillac is an American luxury car make, so Cadillacs are examples of cars.

clue.text: Cheerful air shown by plain lot regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is used

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A jolly tune played by an ordinary crowd, as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' suggests an air that is simple; it is just the letters to pick from.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilt is a light, pleasant rising and falling rhythm, as in a cheerful song.

clue.text: Energetic singer on the way up

indicators.note: on the way up in a down entry means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned over

blocks.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: A lively singer whose career is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' sounds like a rising star; in a down clue it means the word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and keenly enthusiastic, a sense close to energetic.

clue.text: Name left out by nasty team

indicators.note: left out by means omitted from, so the letter is dropped from what follows

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
snide means nasty and sneering

explanation.surface: A player's name is dropped by a spiteful squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team' reads as part of 'nasty team'; it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports team, as in the home side.

clue.text: Refusal by Americans to show sense

blocks.note: no is a refusal
Americans are us, the people of the US

explanation.surface: Americans saying no reveals common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by Americans' reads as who refuses; the 'by' places the American letters beside the refusal. Nous is everyday British slang for practical intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is a British colloquial word for common sense or shrewdness.

clue.text: Stark country largely around mountain and city in Asia

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the country's last letter goes
around means encircling, so these letters wrap the mountain

blocks.note: stark and raw both mean bare, harsh
an alp is a high mountain
the country of India

explanation.surface: A bleak land mostly surrounding a peak and a city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Stark and the shortened country together sit around the mountain. Rawalpindi is a city in northern Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawalpindi is a large Pakistani city near Islamabad, so it is a particular city in Asia.
